mainTopic: The שרצים that make things טמא: the sea mouse, the half-earth mouse and the ערוד, with stories about creatures and their places, and a new משנה on limbs hanging from an animal
overview: The amud begins by finishing a ברייתא about the עכבר (mouse). It shows how the words השורץ, בשרץ and על הארץ in ויקרא 11:29 are each given a job. The half-earth mouse is טמא, a creeper is טמא wherever it creeps, and the sea mouse is left out. One of the Sages offers רבא another way to read the words, and רבא shows it does not hold together. The גמרא then explains that על הארץ is written twice, so it can teach two things. Next, a ברייתא learns from הצב למינהו that the ערוד, נפילים and סלמנדרא are also שרצים, and רבי עקיבא praises ה׳ for making each creature live only in its own world. The גמרא adds that every land creature has a sea version except the חולדה, and it calls the beavers of נרש water creatures. This leads to sharp words about the people of נרש and two other towns. A story tells how a ערוד was born from a snake and a צב as a miraculous punishment. Finally, a new משנה begins about a limb or flesh hanging from a living animal, which can carry טומאת אוכלין once it has had הכשר.

steps.title: The word 'that creep' means anywhere it creeps
steps.stepSummary: The בריתא learns from the word השורץ that creeping animals are טמא wherever they creep, even in the sea.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says 'that creep': this means anywhere that it creeps.
steps.whatsHappening: The בריתא brings a word from the פסוק, השורץ, to show that a שרץ is טמא no matter where it moves around, on land or in the sea.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If השורץ already covers creeping in the sea, then the words 'upon the earth' are left over. Those extra words can then teach that a sea mouse, עכבר של ים, is not part of the טמא mouse category.

keyTerms.meaning: The verse comes to teach, so the verse says
That creeps, a word from the פסוק about creeping animals
A small creeping animal; eight kinds make things טמא
A sea mouse, the subject of this בריתא

steps.whyThisMatters: This reading is what lets 'upon the earth' exclude the sea mouse. The rest of the section defends it.

phrases.english: The verse states: "that creep"
meaning anywhere that it creeps.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the בריתא from before this section, where the meaning of 'upon the earth' was being worked out.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: השורץ teaches that creeping animals are טמא wherever they creep, including in the sea.

steps.title: Maybe 'that creep' means 'that breeds'
steps.stepSummary: The בריתא suggests השורץ could instead mean המשריץ, an animal that breeds. That would leave out a mouse that grows from the earth.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or maybe 'that creep' means only this: any creature that breeds is טמא, and one that does not breed is not. Then I would leave out a mouse that is half flesh and half earth, because it does not reproduce.
steps.whatsHappening: The בריתא challenges the reading in Step 1 by offering another way to read השורץ: as 'one that breeds'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: השורץ and משריץ share the same root, so the word could be about breeding instead of location. If so, it would exclude the mouse that grows half-flesh, half-earth. The word would no longer teach 'anywhere it creeps', and the whole reading from Step 1 falls apart.

keyTerms.meaning: Or maybe it only means, an opening for another reading
One that breeds or produces young
A mouse that is half flesh and half earth, believed to grow out of the ground
Reproduces, has offspring

steps.confusionAlert: The question is not whether this half-earth mouse is a mouse. The question is only what the word השורץ is teaching us.

phrases.english: Or perhaps "that creep" means only this:
one might think that any creature that breeds imparts impurity,
and one that does not breed does not impart impurity?
Then I would exclude a mouse that is half flesh
and half earth, since it does not reproduce.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges Step 1 by offering a rival meaning for the same word.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading of השורץ as 'anywhere it creeps'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The word could just as easily mean 'that breeds', which would exclude the half-earth mouse instead of teaching about location.

steps.title: Logic already includes the half-earth mouse
steps.stepSummary: The בריתא argues from a comparison to the חולדה: just as any animal called חולדה counts, any animal called עכבר counts, even the half-earth one.
steps.simpleTranslation: But this can be worked out by logic. The Torah made the weasel טמא and made the mouse טמא. Just as 'weasel' means anything called a weasel, 'mouse' means anything called a mouse. So I would include the mouse that is half flesh and half earth.
steps.whatsHappening: The בריתא pushes back on Step 2. Logic shows the half-earth mouse is included, so השורץ should not be read as leaving it out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: חולדה and עכבר appear next to each other in the same פסוק, so they are compared. For חולדה, the name alone decides. So for עכבר too, the name alone decides, and the half-earth mouse is called עכבר. This would support Step 1's reading of השורץ.

keyTerms.meaning: But it is a logical argument, it can be worked out by reasoning
Weasel, listed in the same פסוק as the mouse
Just as ... so too ..., a comparison formula
Anything that carries that name

phrases.english: But it is a logical inference:
The Torah made the weasel impure and made the mouse impure;
just as "weasel" means anything called a weasel,
so too "mouse" means anything called a mouse;

phrases.aramaic: אָבִיא עַכְבָּר שֶׁחֶצְיוֹ בָּשָׂר וְחֶצְיוֹ אֲדָמָה.
phrases.english: so I would include a mouse that is half flesh and half earth.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְדִין הוּא: טִימֵּא בְּחוּלְדָּה וְטִימֵּא בְּעַכְבָּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the 'breeding' reading of Step 2 by showing that logic includes the half-earth mouse.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The suggestion that השורץ excludes non-breeding mice
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The comparison to חולדה, based on the name alone, already includes the half-earth mouse.

steps.title: The comparison can be turned the other way
steps.stepSummary: The בריתא shows the חולדה comparison could go the opposite way: a חולדה breeds, so maybe only a breeding עכבר counts.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or go this way: just as a weasel reproduces, so too the mouse must be one that reproduces?
steps.whatsHappening: The בריתא shows that the logic in Step 3 is not decisive. The same comparison can be used to exclude the half-earth mouse. This sets up the need for a verse.
steps.deeperAnalysis: You could compare the two animals by their name, as in Step 3, or by the fact that they breed. Since both ways are possible, logic alone cannot settle the question.

keyTerms.meaning: Go this way instead, turning an argument in the opposite direction

phrases.english: Or go this way:
just as a weasel reproduces,
so too the mouse must be one that reproduces?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Undercuts Step 3's logic by reversing the comparison.
steps.kashyaTarget: The comparison to חולדה based on name
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The comparison could just as well be based on breeding, which would exclude the half-earth mouse.

steps.title: The word 'among the creeping animals' settles it
steps.stepSummary: The extra word בשרץ in the פסוק includes the half-earth mouse, so השורץ keeps its meaning of 'anywhere it creeps'.
steps.simpleTranslation: Therefore the verse says 'among the creeping animals'.
steps.whatsHappening: Since logic could go either way, the בריתא brings a word from the פסוק to decide the question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בשרץ includes the half-earth mouse, so השורץ is not needed to exclude it. That brings back the reading from Step 1: השורץ means anywhere it creeps, including the sea, and 'upon the earth' teaches that the sea mouse is not טמא.

keyTerms.meaning: Among the creeping animals, a word in the same פסוק

steps.whatToRemember: The half-earth mouse is טמא, included by בשרץ. השורץ means 'wherever it creeps', even in the sea. So 'upon the earth' leaves out the עכבר של ים.

phrases.english: Therefore the verse states: "among the creeping animals."
phrases.notes: Same פסוק, ויקרא 11:29. This word brings in the half-earth mouse.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the deadlock of Steps 3-4 with a verse, which restores Step 1.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Brings an extra word from the verse to include the case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: השורץ might mean 'that breeds' and exclude the half-earth mouse.
steps.terutzMaskana: בשרץ includes the half-earth mouse, so השורץ means 'anywhere it creeps', and 'upon the earth' excludes the sea mouse.

steps.title: A Sage suggests a different way to read the words
steps.stepSummary: One of the Sages proposes to רבא: בשרץ includes the half-earth mouse, השורץ includes even a sea mouse, and על הארץ only means a creeper is טמא while it is on land.
steps.simpleTranslation: One of the Sages said to רבא: Why not say that 'among the creeping animals' includes the half-earth mouse, and 'that creep' includes anything that creeps, even a sea mouse? And if you object because of 'upon the earth,' that only means it makes things impure on land, and if it went down into the sea, it does not.
steps.whatsHappening: One of the Sages challenges the בריתא's reading in front of רבא by offering a different way to divide up the words of the פסוק. In his version, a sea mouse would be טמא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The בריתא used השורץ to mean 'wherever it creeps' and used על הארץ to leave out the sea mouse. This Sage gives השורץ a new job: including every creeper, even one that lives in the sea. He then turns על הארץ into a rule about location: on land it is טמא, in the sea it is not.

keyTerms.meaning: Say instead. This introduces a different suggested reading.
To include, to bring in
A sea mouse, a mouse-like creature that lives in the sea
'Upon the earth,' the words in the פסוק describing where the creeper is

phrases.english: One of the Sages said to Rava:
Say: "among the creeping animals"
comes to include a mouse
that is half flesh and half earth;
"that creep" means anything that creeps,
and even a sea mouse.
And if you object because of "upon the earth":
on land it makes things impure;
if it went down into the sea, it does not make things impure.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ הָהוּא מִדְּרַבָּנַן לְרָבָא: אֵימָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts step 5's use of בשרץ for the half-earth mouse, but reassigns השורץ and על הארץ.
steps.kashyaTarget: The בריתא's reading that השורץ means 'wherever it creeps' and that על הארץ leaves out the sea mouse
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same words could be split a different way, making the sea mouse טמא and treating על הארץ as a location rule.

steps.title: רבא shows the suggestion does not make sense
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers: once the Sage's reading includes the sea mouse among the impure creatures, there is no good reason to make it טמא only on land and טהור in its own habitat.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Since you have made the sea a place of impurity, what difference does it make to me whether it is here or there?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא rejects the Sage's suggestion as an unreasonable way to read the verses.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Sage's reading in step 6 includes the sea mouse as a species, but makes both land and sea mice טמא only while on land, and טהור once they go down to the sea. רבא rejects that way of assigning the verses: once the sea species is included, why should its impurity vanish in its own habitat? Rashi calls this an unreasonable reading of the verses, not a self-contradiction.

keyTerms.meaning: You have made it, you have treated it as
A place where impurity can exist

keyTerms.term: מָה לִי הָכָא מָה לִי הָכָא
keyTerms.meaning: What difference is there between here and there? Meaning both cases are the same.

phrases.english: He said to him: But since you have made the sea
a place of impurity,
phrases.notes: He means: your reading includes the sea species among the impure creatures, so why should location remove its טומאה?

phrases.aramaic: מָה לִי הָכָא, מָה לִי הָכָא.
phrases.english: what difference is it to me here, what difference is it to me there?
phrases.notes: Literally 'here' both times. The first means on land and the second means in the sea.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the alternative reading proposed in step 6.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole alternative reading, specifically the claim that על הארץ makes a creeper טהור once it enters the sea
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Unreasonable reading of the verses. Once the sea mouse is included among the impure species, there is no good reason for its own habitat to remove its טומאה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This leaves the בריתא's reading standing: השורץ means wherever it creeps, and על הארץ is what leaves out the sea mouse.

steps.title: The words על הארץ are already needed for something else
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: how can על הארץ be used to leave out the sea mouse, when רב יצחק בר אבדימי uses it to leave out ספק טומאה צפה?
steps.simpleTranslation: But this 'upon the earth' is needed to exclude an uncertain case of floating impurity, as רב יצחק בר אבדימי said: 'upon the earth' comes to exclude an uncertain case of floating impurity!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the use of על הארץ for the sea mouse, because these words already have another job.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A word in the פסוק usually teaches only one thing. רב יצחק בר אבדימי learns from על הארץ that when a person is unsure whether he touched טומאה floating on water, he stays טהור. So על הארץ seems to be used up and cannot also teach about the sea mouse.

keyTerms.meaning: It is needed for, it is already used for something else
To exclude, to leave out
An uncertain case of floating impurity, where one is unsure about contact with טומאה floating on water. The person stays טהור.

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up 'floating impurity' with the sea mouse. These are two separate teachings that both seem to come from the same words על הארץ.

phrases.english: But this "upon the earth"
is needed to exclude
an uncertain case of floating impurity,
phrases.notes: If someone is unsure whether he touched טומאה floating on water, he stays טהור.

phrases.english: as Rav Yitzchak bar Avdimi said:
"Upon the earth" comes to exclude an uncertain case of floating impurity!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: With the Sage's reading rejected, the גמרא now questions the בריתא's own use of על הארץ.
steps.kashyaTarget: Using על הארץ to leave out the sea mouse
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: על הארץ is already used by רב יצחק בר אבדימי for ספק טומאה צפה, so it cannot also teach about the sea mouse.

steps.title: The words על הארץ are written twice
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that על הארץ appears twice in the פסוקים, so one teaches about floating impurity and the other leaves out the sea mouse.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Upon the earth' is written two times.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves the question by pointing out that the words על הארץ show up twice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the phrase is written two times, each one can teach its own lesson. One is used for ספק טומאה צפה, and the other teaches that a sea mouse is not טמא.

keyTerms.meaning: Two
Are written

steps.whatToRemember: השורץ means a creeper is טמא wherever it creeps. בשרץ includes the half-earth mouse. על הארץ is written twice: one teaches about ספק טומאה צפה, and the other leaves out the sea mouse.

phrases.english: "Upon the earth" is written two times.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 8.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Pointing to a second occurrence of the same phrase in the פסוקים
steps.terutzHavaAmina: על הארץ is written only once and is used up by ספק טומאה צפה.
steps.terutzMaskana: על הארץ appears twice, so one teaches ספק טומאה צפה and the other leaves out the sea mouse.

steps.title: The great lizard 'after its kinds' includes more creatures
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that the words הַצָּב לְמִינֵהוּ add the ערוד, the נפילים, and the סלמנדרא to the list of creeping animals.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Sages taught: 'The great lizard after its kinds' comes to include the ערוד, and also the נפילים and the סלמנדרא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that reads the word לְמִינֵהוּ as adding more creatures to the group of טמא creeping animals. This opens a new topic.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה lists eight שרצים, and one of them is הַצָּב. The extra word לְמִינֵהוּ (after its kinds) tells us that similar creatures belong in the same group, so the ערוד, נפילים and סלמנדרא are included too.

keyTerms.meaning: A large lizard, one of the eight שְׁרָצִים in the תורה
After its kinds; this word adds similar species
To include, to bring in something extra
A type of snake-like creeping creature
The salamander

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
"The great lizard after its kinds"
comes to include the arvad,
and also the nefilim and the salamander.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new ברייתא about the list of שרצים, after the discussion of the sea mouse.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The word לְמִינֵהוּ adds the ערוד, נפילים and סלמנדרא to the טמא creeping animals.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא's amazement at creatures bound to their own world
steps.stepSummary: Whenever רבי עקיבא reached this פסוק, he said 'How great are Your works, ה׳.' Creatures of sea and land, or of fire and air, die right away if they move into the other place.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רבי עקיבא reached this verse he would say: 'How great are Your works, ה׳!' You have creatures that grow in the sea and creatures that grow on land. If the sea ones came up onto land, they would die at once. If the land ones went down into the sea, they would die at once. You have creatures that grow in fire and creatures that grow in the air. If the fire ones came up into the air, they would die at once. If the air ones went down into fire, they would die at once. 'How great are Your works, ה׳.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא goes on with a story: רבי עקיבא would burst out in praise of הקב״ה when he learned this פסוק. He describes how every creature can live only in its own place.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Sea creatures die on land and land creatures die in the sea. In the same way, fire creatures die in air and air creatures die in fire. He brings up fire because of the סלמנדרא just mentioned, which was understood to come from fire. Each creature is made exactly for its own world, and that is what amazes רבי עקיבא.

keyTerms.meaning: How great are Your works, ה׳‎ (תְּהִלִּים 104:24)
Creatures
If, were it to happen that
Fire
Dry land

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a הלכה about טומאה. It is praise of הקב״ה, set off by the creatures in the פסוק.

phrases.aramaic: וּכְשֶׁהָיָה רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא מַגִּיעַ לְפָסוּק זֶה,
phrases.english: And when Rabbi Akiva would reach this verse,
he would say: "How great are Your works, ה׳!"
You have creatures that grow in the sea,
and You have creatures that grow on land.
Those in the sea, if they came up onto land, would die at once;
phrases.notes: Some versions say בַּיַּבָּשָׁה in the round brackets; the square brackets give the corrected wording לַיַּבָּשָׁה, meaning 'onto the land'.

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁבַּיַּבָּשָׁה – אִילְמָלֵי יוֹרְדוֹת לַיָּם מִיָּד מֵתוֹת.
phrases.english: those on land, if they went down into the sea, would die at once.
You have creatures that grow in fire,
and You have creatures that grow in the air.

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁבָּאוּר – אִילְמָלֵי עוֹלוֹת לָאֲוִיר מִיָּד מֵתוֹת,
phrases.english: Those in fire, if they came up into the air, would die at once;

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁבָּאֲוִיר – אִילְמָלֵי יוֹרְדוֹת לָאוּר מִיָּד מֵתוֹת.
phrases.english: those in the air, if they went down into fire, would die at once.
"How great are Your works, ה׳."

steps.triggerLanguage: וּכְשֶׁהָיָה רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא מַגִּיעַ לְפָסוּק זֶה, אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא with רבי עקיבא's reaction to the פסוק of הַצָּב לְמִינֵהוּ.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Each creature is bound to its own world (sea, land, fire, or air), and this shows the greatness of הקב״ה's works.

steps.title: Every land creature has a sea version, except the weasel
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that every creature on land has a matching creature in the sea, except the חולדה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Sages taught: Everything that exists on land exists in the sea, except for the weasel.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another ברייתא about land and sea creatures. It gives a general rule and one exception.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This fits the earlier talk of the sea mouse: land creatures have sea versions. The ברייתא adds that the חולדה is the one land creature with no sea version.

keyTerms.meaning: Whatever exists on land exists in the sea
Except for
Weasel

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
Everything that exists on land exists in the sea,
except for the weasel.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: כֹּל שֶׁיֵּשׁ בַּיַּבָּשָׁה יֵשׁ בַּיָּם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new ברייתא on the same theme of creatures and their places, land against sea.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Every land creature has a sea counterpart except the חולדה.

steps.title: רבי זירא finds a verse hinting at the weasel
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא asks what פסוק hints to the weasel rule, and he points to 'Listen, all inhabitants of the חלד'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said: What is the verse for this? 'Listen, all you inhabitants of the world (חֶלֶד).'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא asks for a source for the ברייתא's rule about the חולדה, and he answers with a פסוק from תהלים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word חֶלֶד, a name for the dry land, sounds like חוּלְדָּה. The land is called by the weasel's name because the weasel lives only on land and has no sea version. That supports the exception in the ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the verse (the source for this)?
The world or dry land; it sounds like חוּלְדָּה
Inhabitants, those who dwell

steps.whatToRemember: Every land creature has a sea version except the חולדה, and the land is called חלד after it.

phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira said: What is the verse for this?
"Listen, all you inhabitants of the world (cheled)."
phrases.notes: תהלים 49:2. The land is called חלד after the חולדה, the creature found only on land.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a פסוק as the source for the exception of the חולדה in the ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: The rule that the חולדה has no sea counterpart.
steps.raayaSupportSource: תהלים 49:2, הַאֲזִינוּ כׇּל יֹשְׁבֵי חָלֶד, where the land is named חלד after the חולדה.

steps.title: The beavers of נרש are not land creatures
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע says the beavers of נרש do not count as creatures of the settled land.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא the son of רב יהושע said: The beavers of נרש are not from the settled land.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds one more example to its talk about land creatures and sea creatures. The beavers of נרש are counted as water creatures, not land creatures.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier steps sorted creatures into those of the land and those of the sea. This statement places the beavers of נרש on the water side. So they are not judged as land creatures that creep on the earth.

keyTerms.meaning: Beavers, animals that live in and around water
A town in בבל
The settled, dry land where people live

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ:
phrases.english: Rav Huna the son of Rav Yehoshua said:
The beavers of Neresh
are not from the settled land.
phrases.notes: He means they live in the water, so they are not counted as land creatures.

steps.triggerLanguage: אמר רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another example to the discussion of land creatures and sea creatures.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The beavers of נרש are water creatures and do not count as creatures of the settled land.

steps.title: רב פפא places נרש under a ban
steps.stepSummary: Since נרש was mentioned, רב פפא says the whole town deserves a שמתא, from the most important people to the least.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: Let נרש be under a שמתא: its fat, its hide, and its tail.
steps.whatsHappening: The mention of נרש leads the גמרא off topic for a moment. רב פפא says the people of נרש deserve a ban.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is not about animals. רב פפא uses the picture of a whole animal, its fat, hide and tail, to mean every kind of person in the town.

keyTerms.meaning: A ban, a formal separation from the community
Its fat
Its hide
Its tail

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
Neresh is under a ban,
its fat, its hide, and its tail.
phrases.notes: A picture for the whole town: everybody, from the most important people to the least.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The name נרש in the last step leads to a side discussion about the town's people.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The people of נרש, all of them, deserve a שמתא.

steps.title: רב פפא applies a verse to נרש
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא reads the פסוק 'Land, land, land, hear the word of ה׳' as speaking about נרש, which does not want to listen.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Land, land, land, hear the word of ה׳.' רב פפא said: נרש does not want to hear the word of ה׳.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא keeps going with the side topic of נרש. רב פפא uses a פסוק to describe the town.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק calls on the land three times to listen. רב פפא says this fits נרש, a place that refuses to listen to the word of ה׳.

keyTerms.meaning: Hear! Listen!
Did not want, refused

phrases.english: "O land, land, land, hear the word of the Lord":
Rav Pappa said:
Neresh does not want
to listen to the word of the Lord.

steps.triggerLanguage: ארץ ארץ ארץ שמעי דבר ה׳
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רב פפא's criticism of נרש, now using a פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The פסוק's call to a land that does not listen fits נרש.

steps.title: Warnings about the people of three towns
steps.stepSummary: רב גידל in the name of רב gives three warnings about dishonest people from נרש, נהר פקוד and פומבדיתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב גידל said in the name of רב: If a man from נרש kisses you, count your teeth. If a man from נהר פקוד walks with you, it is because of the nice cloak he sees on you. If a man from פומבדיתא walks with you, change where you are staying.
steps.whatsHappening: The side discussion about נרש goes on. רב gives three sharp warnings about thieves from three towns.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each line is a joke-like warning: the person seems friendly but is really planning to steal. This ends the side discussion about the towns.

keyTerms.meaning: He kisses you
Your teeth
He walks along with you
A cloak or coat
Your lodging, the place where you stay

steps.whatToRemember: The talk about נרש and the other towns is a side topic. It came up only because נרש was mentioned with the beavers.

phrases.english: Rav Giddel said that Rav said:
If a man from Neresh kisses you,
count your teeth;
phrases.notes: Make sure he didn't steal one of them while kissing you!

phrases.english: if a man from Nehar Pekod walks along with you,
it is because of the nice cloak that he sees on you;
if a man from Pumbedita walks along with you,
change your lodging place.

steps.triggerLanguage: אמר רב גידל אמר רב נרשאה נשקיך
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues and closes the side discussion about the people of נרש, adding two more towns.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Be careful with the people of נרש, נהר פקוד and פומבדיתא, since they may be trying to rob you.

steps.title: A snake and a צב produce a ערוד
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא בר תורתא tells how he saw a snake wrapped around a צב, and later a ערוד came out from between them.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא בר תורתא said: Once I went to ועד, and I saw a snake wrapped around a צב. After some time, a ערוד came out from between them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to talking about creatures. רב הונא בר תורתא tells what he saw about where the ערוד comes from.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 10, the words הצב למינהו added the ערוד to the list of creeping animals. This story shows a link between the ערוד and the צב: the ערוד came from a צב and a snake.

keyTerms.meaning: Wrapped around
A type of large lizard
A dangerous creature that comes from a snake and a צב

steps.whyThisMatters: It helps explain why the ערוד is listed together with the צב in the words הצב למינהו.

phrases.english: Rav Huna bar Torta said:
Once I went to Va'ad,
phrases.notes: ועד is the name of a place.

phrases.english: and I saw a snake
that was wrapped around a great lizard;
after some time, an arvad came out from between them.

steps.triggerLanguage: אמר רב הונא בר תורתא פעם אחת הלכתי לוועד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the side topic of the towns and returns to the creatures discussed in step 10.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ערוד comes from a snake and a צב.

steps.title: רבי שמעון החסיד explains the strange creature as a measure-for-measure punishment
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון החסיד tells רב הונא בר תורתא that ה׳ said: they brought a creature I did not create into My world, so I will bring a creature I did not create upon them.
steps.simpleTranslation: And when I came before רבי שמעון החסיד, he said to me: The Holy One, Blessed be He, said: They brought into being a creature that I did not create in My world. So I too will bring upon them a creature that I did not create in My world.
steps.whatsHappening: The story from the last step goes on. רב הונא בר תורתא asked רבי שמעון החסיד about the ערוד he saw, and was told it is a punishment.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The people made a creature that is not part of ה׳'s creation, a mix of two kinds. The punishment matches the sin: ה׳ sends a creature He also did not create, the dangerous ערוד, against them. This is מדה כנגד מדה, punishment that matches the wrongdoing.

keyTerms.meaning: A creature
The pious one, a title given to רבי שמעון
The Holy One, Blessed be He (ה׳)
So too I, which introduces the matching punishment

phrases.english: And when I came before Rabbi Shimon the Pious,

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לִי: אָמַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא:
phrases.english: he said to me: The Holy One, Blessed be He, said:
They brought about a creature
phrases.notes: 'They' are the people who crossbred the snake and the צב.

phrases.english: that I did not create in My world;
so too, I will bring upon them a creature
that I did not create in My world.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the story of רב הונא בר תורתא by giving the meaning of the ערוד he saw.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ערוד is a matching punishment: people made a creature ה׳ did not create, so ה׳ sends such a creature against them.

steps.title: How could a snake and a צב have offspring together?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a rule that animals can only have young together if they mate and carry their young in the same way. A snake and a צב do not, so how was a ערוד born?
steps.simpleTranslation: But didn't the Master say: Any animals whose mating and pregnancy are the same can give birth to and raise young with each other. Any animals whose mating and pregnancy are not the same cannot give birth to and raise young with each other.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the story. A known rule says this crossbreed should be impossible.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule says two kinds can have young together only if their mating and the length of their pregnancy are the same. A snake and a צב are not alike in this way. So the story of a ערוד coming from the two of them seems to go against nature.

keyTerms.meaning: Mating
Pregnancy, the time the young are carried before birth
They give birth and raise young

phrases.english: But didn't the Master say:
All animals whose mating and pregnancy are the same
can give birth and raise young from one another;
and all whose mating and pregnancy are not the same
cannot give birth and raise young from one another.
phrases.notes: The challenge is left unsaid: a snake and a צב are not the same in this way.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions whether the crossbreed described in the story could really have happened.
steps.kashyaTarget: The story that a ערוד came from a snake and a צב.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Animals that do not mate and carry young in the same way cannot have offspring together, and a snake and a צב are such animals.

steps.title: רב: it was a miracle within a miracle
steps.stepSummary: רב answers that the birth of the ערוד was not natural. It was a double miracle.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: It was a miracle within a miracle!
steps.whatsHappening: רב answers the challenge. Yes, nature would not allow this, so it happened through a miracle.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule about mating and pregnancy stays true. This case was an exception that happened through a miracle, so the story does not go against the rule.

keyTerms.meaning: A miracle
A miracle inside a miracle, a double miracle

phrases.english: Rav says: A miracle within a miracle!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge about how the crossbreed was possible.
steps.terutzResolutionType: The case is an exception: it happened through a miracle, not through nature.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The story cannot be true, because nature does not allow such offspring.
steps.terutzMaskana: The rule of nature stays true; this birth happened through a double miracle.

steps.title: But this was a punishment, so why call it a miracle?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how something harmful, the birth of a dangerous creature, can be called a miracle.
steps.simpleTranslation: But this is a punishment!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions רב's word 'miracle'. A miracle sounds like something good, but the ערוד brought harm.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We usually use the word נס for a good thing ה׳ does to save people. Here the result was a dangerous creature, so the word seems out of place.

keyTerms.meaning: A punishment, a disaster

phrases.english: This is a punishment?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the word 'miracle' that רב used in the answer.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's description of the event as נס בתוך נס.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A miracle is something good, but the birth of the ערוד was a harmful event.

steps.title: It was a miracle meant for punishment
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that 'miracle within a miracle' means a supernatural event whose purpose was to punish.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does 'a miracle within a miracle' mean? A miracle for punishment.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains רב's words. A miracle does not have to be for good; this one was sent to punish.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word נס here means an event above nature, not necessarily a good one. This fits רבי שמעון החסיד's explanation in step 19: ה׳ made it happen to punish the people who made the crossbreed.

keyTerms.meaning: For the sake of punishment

steps.whatToRemember: The ערוד came from a snake and a צב only through a miracle, and that miracle was a matching punishment for the people who made a creature ה׳ did not create.

phrases.english: What is meant by 'a miracle within a miracle'?
For punishment.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge to רב's wording and closes the discussion of the ערוד.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains what the word means: נס here is a supernatural event, not necessarily a good one.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A miracle must be a good thing, so a harmful event cannot be called a miracle.
steps.terutzMaskana: It was a miracle whose purpose was punishment.

steps.title: New משנה: a limb or flesh hanging off an animal
steps.stepSummary: The משנה teaches that a limb or flesh hanging loosely from an animal can carry טומאת אוכלין while still attached, but first it needs הכשר.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: A limb or flesh that is hanging loose on an animal can pass on the טומאה of food while still in its place, and it needs הכשר.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins with a new topic. It is about a limb or a piece of flesh that is partly cut off and still hanging from a living animal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even though the piece is still attached to the animal, it is treated like food for טומאה. It can become טמא and pass on טומאת אוכלין right where it hangs. Like all food, it can only become טמא after it has had הכשר, meaning it got wet with one of the liquids that make food able to become טמא.

keyTerms.meaning: Short for מתניתין, our משנה
The limb, a full part of the body with flesh, sinews and bone
Hanging loose, partly cut off but still attached
The kind of טומאה that food carries and passes on
In their place, while still attached to the animal
Making food able to become טמא, by its getting wet with one of the special liquids

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think a hanging limb counts as part of the living animal and so cannot become טמא as food. The משנה says it can carry טומאת אוכלין even while still attached.
steps.whyThisMatters: This משנה opens the next topic. The גמרא will now discuss how the law treats a piece that is still partly attached to a living animal.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
The limb and the flesh that are hanging loose from the animal
impart impurity as food while still in their place,
and they need to be made able to become impure.
phrases.notes: They first have to get wet with one of the liquids that let food become טמא.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new משנה with a new topic, not connected to the story of the ערוד.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A limb or flesh hanging from a living animal can carry טומאת אוכלין while still attached, once it has had הכשר.
